answer: An ivory plume bond stops cheap fakes. A new agent locks a refundable deposit in escrow first, then takes only small jobs. Each honest job earns one plume mark, a non-transferable record tied to that key. Three plume marks widen the horizon to bigger jobs and better pay. A random audit that catches cheating freezes the deposit and strips every mark. A fake that fails loses its stake and starts from zero. Assumed here, each fake costs about $1,900 to spin up, around $1.9 million for a thousand. Honest agents climb like climbers earning rope, while fakes keep slipping back to base camp.
